units: SI: metre, kilogram, second, radian; angles explicitly suffixed _deg are degrees
description: Generic DN25 handle ball valve based on selected Bray Flow-Tek 7100 DN25 catalogue dimensions and a simplified flat lever. No manufacturer CAD or converted mesh is embedded.

pipe.provenance: 33.7 mm outside diameter and 700 mm section length are task settings; bore, thread and flow are omitted.

ball.name: Bray-reference generic DN25 ball valve
ball.reference_product: Bray Flow-Tek 7000 series / 7100 threaded full-port, RPTFE seats
ball.safety_trigger_state: fixed unlocked / manufacturer-described bypass; trigger action omitted

provenance.catalogue_dimensions: Bray 7000/8000 brochure, page 10, DN25: A=92 mm for NPT/SW/BW, D=200 mm shaft-to-handle-end, C=87 mm pipe-axis-to-highest-point, C1=52 mm pipe-axis-to-mounting-top. H/J=35.7 mm are mounting hole spacings, not heights.
provenance.contact_shape_reference: Generic bent flat metal lever with a thin blue cover, flat through the tip. Width 20 mm, covered total thickness 6 mm, metal plate 3 mm and bend positions are task assumptions, not Bray measurements.
provenance.assumptions: Body radii, rounded bolt envelopes, detailed cast shape, covered grip cross-section, bend location, moving mass/inertia and contact friction are simplified task settings. Simplified exterior only; internal ball, seals, threads, fluid and pressure omitted. Safety trigger held in the manufacturer-described bypass state; unlocking not part of this task.

joint_convention.note: Increasing q closes about the negative outward stem axis. Station XML files use metres and radians.

sources.note: Bray-based generic task geometry, not an exact manufacturer replica or a model calibrated from measured real-valve data.
sources.bray_dimensions_reference: Page 10, DN25, A=92, C=87, C1=52, D=200 mm; 7100 threaded end on page 11

resistance.model: MuJoCo passive dry-friction constraint; a static breakaway bound and an angle/direction-dependent moving bound, with rest/motion hysteresis. The actual force is read from the solver, never inferred from this configured bound.

ball.magnitude_source: Bray TB1005, page 3: DN25 full-port two-way ball valve with RPTFE seats, 0 bar line pressure, basic torque 14 N*m. Used as the task breakaway reference for the Bray Flow-Tek 7000/7100 dimension-reference valve. This is manufacturer actuator-sizing guidance, not a direct measurement of our valve or a universal DN25 standard value; application and operation-frequency factors may change real requirements.
ball.shape_source: Bray TB1005, page 11: typical floating-ball valve curve in both opening and closing directions, break torque 100%, running approximately 75%, ending approximately 90%. MSS SP-91-2025 provides broader qualitative guidance; it does not specify a universal DN25 torque.
ball.shape_assumptions: The model uses the manufacturer typical 100/75/90 percent ratios in both directions. Smooth initial transitions span 15% of travel and end rises span 22%; these transition positions, interpolation, static re-entry and friction hysteresis are task assumptions, not digitized or individually measured Bray curves. With scale=1, nominal break/run/end levels are 14/10.5/12.6 N*m.

parameter_notes.scale: Nonnegative load multiplier. Does not change robot motor caps.
parameter_notes.solref_solimp: Numerical regularization settings, not material properties.
parameter_notes.hysteresis: Motion begins above 0.02 rad/s; static mode returns only below 0.003 rad/s for 0.1 s. These are numerical task assumptions and must be reported as such.
parameter_notes.limits: Joint stops are set by the scene and handled separately from friction. Ball close-angle variation of 87-92 degrees is a task setting, not a measured closing angle.
parameter_notes.not_modelled: No fluid, pressure-dependent forces, wear, seal leakage, thermal behavior, or real tactile measurements. Any contact/friction force recorded is a simulation result.
parameter_notes.reference_condition: Ball default reference: Bray full-port DN25, RPTFE seats, line pressure 0 bar; fluid dynamics and pressure are not simulated. Reference torque is not a certified capability or a measurement of an individual valve.
